name: Yala
rootCause: On September 14, the stablecoin protocol Yala disclosed that a recent security incident occurred when a hacker abused a temporary deployment key during the setup of an authorized cross-chain bridge. The attacker deployed an unauthorized bridge and extracted 7.64 million USDC (approximately 1,636 ETH). On October 29, the suspect involved in the case was arrested by law enforcement in Bangkok, Thailand, and most of the affected funds have been successfully recovered.

descriptions.text: On September 14, the stablecoin protocol Yala disclosed that a recent security incident occurred when a hacker abused a temporary deployment key during the setup of an authorized cross-chain bridge. The attacker deployed an unauthorized bridge and extracted 7.64 million USDC (approximately 1,636 ETH). On October 29, the suspect involved in the case was arrested by law enforcement in Bangkok, Thailand, and most of the affected funds have been successfully recovered.

Yala’s Bitcoin-backed YU stablecoin lost its peg on 2025-09-14 after an attacker reportedly minted large quantities of unbacked YU on Polygon and sold bridged tokens on Ethereum and Solana. Public reporting attributes the incident to compromised deployment credentials and unauthorized bridge configuration, with approximately $7.6 million to $7.7 million extracted in USDC. Available reporting attributes the incident to compromised deployment or deployer credentials associated with Yala’s cross-chain deployment and bridge configuration process.
